## Fraud Detection Framework  
### Detection Methods  
**1. Real-Time Transaction Monitoring (Fraud Detection Engine)**  
**See:** [[systems]] Fraud Detection Engine (FDE-001)  
**Rules Monitored:**
- Large transaction amount (>£5,000)
- Velocity checks (>5 transactions in 1 hour)
- Geographic anomaly (transaction in different country within 2 hours)
- New beneficiary with large transfer
- Unusual merchant/category
- Cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer
- Multiple failed authentication attempts  
**Action:** Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)  
**2. Manual Review**  
**Triggers for Manual Investigation:**
- Customer reports suspected fraud
- Unusual account activity
- Pattern changes (normal behavior deviation)
- High-value transaction
- Regulatory alert (sanctions, AML)  
**Review Process:**
- Financial Crime team analyzes activity
- Customer contacted for explanation (if safe)
- Transaction approved or blocked based on risk  
**3. Fraud Pattern Analysis**  
**Advanced Analytics:**
- Machine learning model learns normal customer behavior
- Anomalies flagged for review
- Recurring fraud patterns identified
- Fraud perpetrators tracked across customers  
**Feedback Loop:**
- Confirmed fraud updates model
- False positives refined
- Model continuously improves

raw_entities.name: Fraud Detection Framework
raw_entities.description: A comprehensive policy governing the bank's fraud detection methods, including real-time transaction monitoring, manual review procedures, and advanced pattern analysis. The framework establishes detection rules, alert generation protocols, and continuous model improvement through machine learning feedback loops.

raw_entities.name: Real-Time Transaction Monitoring
raw_entities.description: Mandatory requirement to monitor all transactions in real-time using the Fraud Detection Engine (FDE-001) against a defined set of fraud detection rules. Transactions meeting alert criteria are placed on hold for up to 5 days pending review.
context: Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)

raw_entities.name: Large Transaction Amount Detection Rule
raw_entities.description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting for transactions exceeding £5,000. This rule is part of the real-time transaction monitoring framework.

raw_entities.name: Velocity Check Detection Rule
raw_entities.description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when a customer initiates more than 5 transactions within a 1-hour period. This rule identifies potentially fraudulent rapid transaction patterns.

raw_entities.name: Geographic Anomaly Detection Rule
raw_entities.description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when a transaction occurs in a different country within 2 hours of a previous transaction. This rule identifies impossible travel scenarios.
context: Geographic anomaly (transaction in different country within 2 hours)

raw_entities.name: New Beneficiary Large Transfer Detection Rule
raw_entities.description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when a customer initiates a large transfer to a newly added beneficiary. This rule identifies potential account compromise or fraud.

raw_entities.name: Unusual Merchant or Category Detection Rule
raw_entities.description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting for transactions with unusual merchant types or spending categories that deviate from customer's normal behavior.

raw_entities.name: Cash Withdrawal Followed by Large Transfer Detection Rule
raw_entities.description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when a cash withdrawal is immediately followed by a large transfer. This rule identifies potential money laundering or fraud patterns.
context: Cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer

raw_entities.name: Multiple Failed Authentication Attempts Detection Rule
raw_entities.description: Mandatory detection rule requiring monitoring and alerting when multiple failed authentication attempts occur on an account. This rule identifies potential account takeover attempts.

raw_entities.name: Transaction Hold on Fraud Alert
raw_entities.description: Mandatory requirement to place transactions on hold for up to 5 days when a fraud alert is generated by the Fraud Detection Engine, pending manual review and approval.
context: Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)

raw_entities.name: Manual Review of Suspected Fraud
raw_entities.description: Mandatory requirement for the Financial Crime team to manually investigate transactions triggered by customer fraud reports, unusual account activity, pattern changes, high-value transactions, or regulatory alerts. Customer contact for explanation is required when safe to do so.
context: Transaction approved or blocked based on risk

raw_entities.name: Machine Learning Model Training on Confirmed Fraud
raw_entities.description: Mandatory requirement to update the machine learning fraud detection model with confirmed fraud cases to continuously improve detection accuracy and reduce false positives.

raw_entities.name: Fraud Detection Engine
raw_entities.description: Real-time automated system that monitors all transactions against defined fraud detection rules including large amounts, velocity checks, geographic anomalies, new beneficiaries, unusual merchants, and authentication failures. Generates alerts and places flagged transactions on hold.
context: Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)

raw_entities.name: Machine Learning Fraud Pattern Analysis
raw_entities.description: Advanced analytics control that uses machine learning to learn normal customer behavior patterns, flag anomalies for review, identify recurring fraud patterns, and track fraud perpetrators across multiple customers. The model is continuously refined based on confirmed fraud feedback.
context: Machine learning model learns normal customer behavior

raw_entities.name: Financial Crime Team
raw_entities.description: The Financial Crime team is responsible for conducting manual investigations of fraud alerts and suspicious activities, analyzing customer activity, contacting customers for explanations when safe to do so, and making transaction approval or blocking decisions based on risk assessment.
context: Transaction approved or blocked based on risk

raw_entities.name: Fraud
raw_entities.description: The primary risk category addressed by this policy. Fraud encompasses unauthorized transactions, account takeover, new beneficiary fraud, velocity-based fraud, geographic anomalies, and other deceptive activities that the detection framework is designed to identify and prevent.

raw_entities.name: Account Takeover
raw_entities.description: A specific fraud risk where unauthorized parties gain control of a customer account, typically identified through multiple failed authentication attempts and unusual transaction patterns.

raw_entities.name: Money Laundering
raw_entities.description: A financial crime risk identified through the detection of cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer patterns, which may indicate attempts to obscure the origin of funds.
context: Cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer

raw_entities.name: Fraud Detection Alert
raw_entities.description: An automated alert generated by the Fraud Detection Engine when a transaction meets one or more fraud detection rules. The alert triggers transaction hold and manual review by the Financial Crime team.
context: Alert generated, transaction placed on hold (up to 5 days)

raw_entities.name: High-Value Transaction
raw_entities.description: Transactions exceeding £5,000 that are subject to real-time monitoring and fraud detection rules. These transactions are flagged for potential fraud review.

raw_entities.name: Rapid Velocity Transaction
raw_entities.description: Multiple transactions (more than 5) initiated within a 1-hour period that trigger fraud detection alerts due to unusual velocity patterns.

raw_entities.name: Geographic Anomaly Transaction
raw_entities.description: A transaction occurring in a different country within 2 hours of a previous transaction, flagged as a geographic anomaly that may indicate fraud or account compromise.
context: Geographic anomaly (transaction in different country within 2 hours)

raw_entities.name: New Beneficiary Transfer
raw_entities.description: A large transfer to a newly added beneficiary that is subject to fraud detection monitoring and manual review.

raw_entities.name: Cash Withdrawal Followed by Large Transfer
raw_entities.description: A transaction pattern consisting of a cash withdrawal immediately followed by a large transfer, flagged as a potential money laundering or fraud indicator.
context: Cash withdrawal followed by immediate large transfer
